usage: boardwise [-h] [--version]
                 {review,checkup,need-datasheet,triage,triage-batch,review-evidence,review-read,review-eval,bridge,review-mark,edit,doctor,install-skill,compare,draw,persistence,lint,parts,bom,pintable,validate,arch,intent,config} ...

AI harness for EasyEDA Pro: offline design review (stage 1).

positional arguments:
  {review,checkup,need-datasheet,triage,triage-batch,review-evidence,review-read,review-eval,bridge,review-mark,edit,doctor,install-skill,compare,draw,persistence,lint,parts,bom,pintable,validate,arch,intent,config}
    review              Review an EasyEDA .enet netlist or .epro2 backup
                        offline.
    checkup             One-command review: read the live project, report what
                        tier it used.
    need-datasheet      Mark a device/pin the review cannot explain yet, so the
                        report stops short of a pass (058 ⓪: ask for the
                        datasheet before judging it).
    triage              Record the verdict for one warning of an existing
                        `checkup` report (有益/有害/无害 + reason, or needs-manual
                        where the source gave no per-item text), so a re-run
                        cannot drop it (issue #12).
    triage-batch        Apply a whole batch of warning verdicts to an existing
                        `checkup` report in one atomic step (537D1b1): every row
                        is checked and applied in memory first, so one bad row
                        writes nothing at all.
    review-evidence     Collect the live schematic/PCB evidence for an existing
                        `checkup` report and merge it into that report's
                        evidence ledger (537C3b2).
    review-read         Read one existing `checkup` report as structured JSON —
                        one of the questions a review asks (537D1a).
    review-eval         Measure review rules against oracle annotation sets
                        (task 011a).
    bridge              Live channel to a running EasyEDA (daemon + editor
                        extension).
    review-mark         Draw a `boardwise review` pass on the live schematic
                        canvas (012v2 §八: markers + jump list).
    edit                Review-to-local-edit (task 016): turn one review finding
                        into an authorised, verified change of a single
                        component's value.
    doctor              Check that this installation can do anything (daemon ·
                        extension · versions · project).
    install-skill       Copy the bundled SKILL.md into the user-level skill
                        directory of each agent harness (Kimi Code, Claude
                        Code), or — with --agent — print the prompt that has any
                        other harness's AI install it itself.
    compare             Compare a candidate .epro2 against the golden board, per
                        pin (task 005). With --spec the candidate side is the
                        **spec netlist** assembled from block templates instead
                        of a file (task 008a). Exit 0 equal / 1 differences / 2
                        bad input.
    draw                Redraw a golden board on a blank schematic page through
                        the bridge and diff the result per pin (task 006). With
                        --spec the plan is assembled from block templates
                        instead of replayed from the golden page (task 008a),
                        and the spec first passes the product validation gates —
                        a refused spec draws nothing (009-M0). Exit 0 equal / 1
                        differences or failures / 2 bad input / 3 a write's
                        outcome is unknown (a timeout or a dropped connection),
                        which outranks 0 and 1 — the page's state cannot be
                        stated.
    persistence         Snapshot the live page and compare it across a real
                        close-and-reopen (read-only). Exit 0 the snapshot's
                        content survived / 1 it is missing or changed / 2 bad
                        input / 3 undecidable.
    lint                Offline layout lint of the plan (overlap / out-of-frame
                        / through-part / floating or stacked names). No bridge,
                        no editor. Exit 0 clean / 1 violations.
    parts               The curated part library (task 008b): offline selection
                        from blocklib/parts.json, with an explicit --online
                        catalog compare.
    bom                 The bill of materials a board spec implies (task 008c):
                        a BOM is an output of the design, so it is derived from
                        the spec and the shelf.
    pintable            The firmware pin table (task 008c): what the MCU is
                        wired to, read from firmware and cross-checked against
                        the CubeMX .ioc baseline.
    validate            Run a board spec through the validation gates of task
                        008c item 4 (sources, pin budget, levels, power tree;
                        --benchmark adds the closed book). Exit 0 clean / 1
                        blocked / 2 bad input. An undecidable result blocks like
                        a violation does; a skipped gate says so instead of
                        passing.
    arch                Offline: the architecture skeleton for an export (task
                        044 M1) — power tree / analog chains / control chains /
                        buses / intent slots, every judgement a tool cannot make
                        left as a TODO slot.
    intent              The DesignIntent contract's rails: `intent audit` lists
                        the power nets whose voltage only the engineer knows
                        (issue #65), `intent set-rail` writes one answer into
                        the contract with provenance user_stated.
    config              User-level settings in ~/.boardwise/config.json (039
                        批②). `config get <key>` / `config set <key> <value>` /
                        `config show`. Exit 0 ok / 2 bad key, bad value or
                        unreadable file.

need-datasheet.description: The ⓪ 先问再判 step's input (issue #8). Records what the reviewer cannot establish from the drawing and the material at hand — a pin whose function is unknown, a whole device whose behaviour has to be read out of its datasheet — and merges it into the `needs_datasheet` section of an existing `checkup` report. The report's gate is then recomputed: `completion.verdict` becomes `incomplete`, `summary.conclusion` says how many pins are waiting, and `report.md` is re-rendered with the section that forbids claiming a pass while it is non-empty. Idempotent per `(part, pin)`: marking again updates the reason instead of adding a row. Purely offline — no editor, no daemon. Exit 0 applied / 2 bad input / 3 no report.json to mark up.

  --out DIR             The `checkup --out` directory holding report.json (and
                        the sidecar needs-datasheet.json). Default: checkup.
  --part REF            The designator whose function is not established (e.g.
                        U7). Required unless --merge is used.
  --pins P1,P2          Pin names (or numbers) that cannot be explained;
                        repeatable, and each value may be a comma/space list.
                        **Merge semantics** (516 B2): a later call for the same
                        designator takes the **union** of its pins and the ones
                        already recorded — it does not replace them. Omit it for
                        'the whole device'. Use --replace-pins to overwrite

                        pins.

triage.description: xianyuyijinban's step ② as an action: one warning, one verdict, one reason. Writes the verdict into `warning_triage[]` of an existing `checkup` report **and** into the sidecar `warning-triage.json` beside it — which is what makes the judgement survive the next `checkup` (issue #12: the slots were the only AI channel with no way back in). The report's gate is recomputed on the spot: `completion.warningsPendingTriage` drops, `report.md` is re-rendered with the verdict in the table. Idempotent per `key`: a second run for the same key updates it rather than adding a row. **537B: a slot whose `text` is empty (the host's ERC totals, no per-item text) cannot be closed with the three words** — `有益/有害/无害` answer 「这条警告说的是什么」 and need the warning's own text, so the command refuses by name and writes nothing; `needs-manual` is the verdict for those, it takes the same `--reason`, and the row stays in `warningsPendingTriage` (counted apart as `warningsNeedsManual`). Purely offline — no editor, no daemon. Exit 0 applied / 2 bad input (including a key the report does not carry, or a three-word verdict on a text-less slot) / 3 no report.json to triage.

review-evidence.description: The 537C fix for a review that read the live schematic, failed to read the live PCB and produced no PCB image — with none of it disclosed. This command opens the editor through the bridge, runs `engines.liveevidence.collect_live_evidence` once (doc.list identity, then per-document doc.open → document.current focus proof → readback/netlist/geometry/render, focus restored in `finally`), writes the whole capture to `<out>/live-evidence.json` with its bytes/sha256, and merges it into `<out>/report.json`'s `evidence` section through `merge_live_capture` (four live channels replaced, archive/datasheets untouched, identity/focus disclosures added). `report.json`, `report.md` and `board-report.md` are then re-written from that one report reading. It **never** rewrites `review-summary.md`: what a human wrote there is not this command's to replace. The board-level conclusion (`completion`, `summary`, `conclusion`) is not changed — collecting evidence is not judging the board. Paths: --project/--instance choose the editor window (023), --page/--pcb may be repeated to collect an explicit subset (an explicit subset is disclosed as `missing` coverage, never `ok`). Purely read-only actions; no design write. Exit codes describe **this collection**: 0 = the collector returned ok, the identity was verified against the report (`source.project.projectUuid`) and the original focus was restored (a channel with nothing to read, e.g. no PCB document, is `not-applicable` and does not block) · 1 = the collector returned but some direct evidence failed/missing, the selection was an explicit subset, the identity was not verified (including a report with no project uuid) or the focus was not restored · 2 = unusable input (no/broken report, an evidence section of another schema, a merge that refuses the capture, a report that cannot be written) · 3 = nothing may be stated (no `report.json`, the daemon cannot be reached, or `doc.list` itself failed — the capture and its failure disclosure still land). 0 is not a board pass: the board conclusion stays `report.json`'s `conclusion`.

review-read.description: The 537D fix for the review's worst habit: every question about a report was answered by a hand-written one-off JSON parser, and a missing key read as 「零问题」. This command is the one structured read, and it projects — it never re-gates, renders or writes the report. `--section` is one of: verdict / findings / crossView / coverage / artifacts / netlist. `verdict` is `report.conclusion` and nothing else (a report without it is `status: "missing"`; `summary.conclusion` is a sentence and is never promoted to a verdict). `findings` carries the findings list and the triage ledger with `warningsPendingTriage` / `warningsNeedsManual` counted through checkup's own predicates — a `needs-manual` row stays pending. `crossView` copies every board's `crossView` verbatim (`checked: false`, `suspected` and the candidate mappings included) and says `missing` when there is none. `coverage` copies the environment/evidence ledgers and names every absent section in `missingSections` instead of guessing it. `netlist` projects the live capture's own parsed netlist (components, nets, pin names) in sorted order, and answers `missing` with a reason when the capture did not verify, the live schematic is not `ok`, or no netlist artifact was cited; a cited netlist that fails its bytes/sha256/UTF-8/parse proof is exit 2. `artifacts` lists every file the report's machine fields cite (canvas images, channel artifacts, the live capture's own files, then the five standard outputs) with `path`/`exists`/`bytesOnDisk`/`bytesMatch`/`sha256Matches`/`error` per row, `missingOutputs` for absent standard outputs, and a final `status` of ok / missing / unavailable; a citation outside `--out` is refused before it is read. bridge.description: Live channel to a running EasyEDA Pro: a loopback daemon plus an editor extension. Actions owned by 'daemon' are answered locally; 'connector' actions are forwarded into the editor.
bridge.epilog:
actions:

action                 owner      risk    params                       summary
hello                  daemon     read    token,role,protocol,client   Handshake. Must be the first frame on every connection.
ping                   daemon     read    -                            Liveness check; answered by the daemon, not forwarded.
document.current       connector  read    -                            Which project / document / document type is open in the editor.
sys.probe              connector  read    checks,namespace,namespaces,functionsOnly,call,realm READ-ONLY introspection of the editor's live API surface: the editor version, the namespaces bound on `eda`, and what each requested namespace actually exposes. Exists because the type package declaring a method and the running editor exposing it are different statements. Two modes: `checks` verifies named members with a plain `typeof ns[name]` read (immune to the exotic host objects that abort enumeration), and enumeration finds members nobody predicted.
sys.self_update        connector  dangerous bundleB64,version,confirm,reload Replace this connector's bundle in the editor's extension IndexedDB (User_<teamUuid>_v6, store names are EasyEDA-internal) and reload the page, so a new build takes effect WITHOUT uninstall/import/restart. The response is sent before the reload fires. Only `config.version` and `fileSize` are touched in the index record — the external-interaction grant is preserved. Every step validates; any failure is an explicit error (fall back to a manual reinstall), never a silent degrade. `reload: false` (528A) writes the same records and schedules no reload: the stored build stays dormant until the editor re-evaluates the extension.
sys.identity           connector  read    -                            READ-ONLY: the editor's two identity layers, and whether they agree (018 §B). Returns the project the editor reports as focused, the project the *active document* belongs to (from getCurrentDocumentInfo's parentProjectUuid, or the document's own per-kind info read), a `consistent` flag comparing the two, and the active page's uuid. Exists because the two layers disagreed on the machine (2026-09-21): `doc.open`, which addresses the pages of the project the editor has open, refused a uuid whose document was in front — so a caller about to write needs to be able to ask this first. `consistent` is **null** (with `consistentBasis`) when the comparison cannot be made, never a hopeful true.
sys.get_document_file  connector  read    fileType,fileName,password,timeoutMs READ-ONLY: the open document as an .epro/.epro2 archive, base64. The online half of the offline review pipeline — the bytes are the same kind of archive `boardwise review` reads, so they go through load_epru_text -> build_schematic_model with no rule changes. The declaration gates the call on 工程设计图 > 文件导出 and says a missing grant throws every time; the connector cannot read grants, so a refusal carries the host's own message plus the documented gates in `detail.permissions`. `isZip` is reported rather than assumed.
sys.get_project_file   connector  read    fileType,fileName,password,timeoutMs READ-ONLY: the open **project** as one .epro/.epro2 archive, base64 — every page, every library document and the PCB in a single payload, which is why 025 batch 2's data path tries it first (tier `project-file`). Gated on 工程管理 > 下载工程, a **different** gate from getDocumentFile's 工程设计图 > 文件导出, so "the document export works" does not imply this one does; a refusal carries the host's message plus the gate the declaration names for this call. `scope` says which archive the caller actually got.
sys.get_document_source connector  read    maxChars,uuid                READ-ONLY: one document's own source text, unjudged. The declaration is one line (`Promise<string | undefined>`, @beta) and says nothing about the format, so whether it equals the .epru record stream inside an .epro2 is a question for a probe, not for this action. Truncates to `maxChars` and echoes both ends of the text (the head, plus `tail` when truncated), because a stream is recognised by its first and last records. `uuid` is honoured or refused: the host's `getDocumentSource()` takes no arguments (measured arity 0 on EDA 3.2.186), so it reads the **active** document and nothing else — asking for any other uuid is `DOC_NOT_ACTIVE` (open it with `doc.open` first), never a silent return of the wrong document's source (179, the hole 178b's probe filed). Omitting `uuid` reads whatever is active. Every answer names the document it read (R1-2): `uuid` / `name` / `type` as the project's document listing spells them, or all three null with a `notes` line when the focus moved during the read.
sys.set_document_source connector  dangerous source,uuid,confirm          **RECON ONLY, DANGEROUS**: rewrite the **active** document's source text. The write half of the source channel (R1-3): 178b/179 measured that the bridge could read a document's source but nothing could write one, so whether `doc.rename`'s NOT_SUPPORTED on 3.2.186 is repairable through the source was unmeasurable. Intended use is a scratch page of the test project (create → rewrite → read back → delete; outputs/R1/runbook.md §R1-3) — the discipline is the caller's, because `setDocumentSource` replaces a whole document's text in one call. `uuid` is required and must be the active document (179's DOC_NOT_ACTIVE shape): the host call takes the text and nothing else (declared arity 1), so it rewrites whatever is in front. `risk=dangerous` puts it behind the create gate's choke point — the daemon refuses it unless `params.confirm is True` and strips the flag. A `true` is read back (`readBack: identical|differs|unreadable`) rather than trusted; anything but `true` is a failure naming the host's own answer.
sch.drc_check          connector  read    strict,userInterface,includeVerboseError READ-ONLY: the schematic DRC, via sch_Drc.check(strict, userInterface, includeVerboseError). The answer's shape changed between editor generations, and both are read (038 O3a/O3b): the 025 §0 measurement (V3) found **aggregate counts only** — `[{type: 'fatalError'|'error'|'warn', count}]`, the per-item detail going to the bottom panel, which has no read interface; the V4.1.93 measurement (2026-10-31, two pages of the test project) found **one object per finding** — `{type, rule, primitives}` with no `count`, 519 of them. The connector normalises both: `entryShape` says which shape answered, `total`/`byType` sum the recognised entries, and `items` keeps the per-item objects verbatim. The host array is still returned **verbatim** under `counts`; an entry with a numeric `count` contributes that count and is never split, a legal-severity entry without one contributes 1, and anything else is counted in `unparsed` instead of folding in as zero. `passed` is `null` (unknown) as soon as any entry was unparsed. A boolean answer is reported as mode `boolean`, never as an empty result. Throws on a page that is not a schematic page, and the throw is reported with the focused document named.
pcb.drc_check          connector  read    strict,userInterface,includeVerboseError,maxChars READ-ONLY: the PCB DRC, per item, via pcb_Drc.check(strict, userInterface, includeVerboseError) — the one DRC that hands back item-level detail (025 §0, and measured 2026-09-23: the tree is group.list[].list[] with leaves carrying ruleName / errorType / explanation.str / obj1 / obj2 / globalIndex / parentId, and every node states its own `count`). Groups are returned **verbatim** so a Finding-mapping layer can read the shape the editor really produces; `counts` only describes what came back, and whole groups are dropped (never cut in half) to stay inside `maxChars`. A non-PCB page is kept distinct from a clean board: the declaration promises `undefined`, the host actually **throws** (a message-bus error — the check publishes to the PCB canvas topic and nothing subscribes on a schematic page), and both are reported as `checked: false` with the focused document named — never as an empty result. Note that an *empty* PCB is not a clean board with zero findings either: the test project's empty PCB answered one 'Netlist Error / Import Changes'.
pcb.drc_ruleset        connector  read    maxChars,all                 READ-ONLY: the DRC rule set in force on the focused PCB, via the read-side members of pcb_Drc — getCurrentRuleConfigurationName(), getCurrentRuleConfiguration(), getDefaultRuleConfigurationName(), getRealTimeDrcStatus() (`all: true` adds getAllRuleConfigurations()). A PCB DRC result is a statement about a rule set, so 025's leaves without these are half an answer. The values come back **verbatim**, sanitised conservatively: functions dropped (they are the back-references that make an editor object graph cyclic), `toJSON`-bearing objects rendered through the host's own serialiser (a Date stays the instant it is), cycles cut as '(cycle)' at the re-entry point; every cut is counted and named in `notes`. **Nothing is compared** — whether a rule set matches the board's process is a judgement the review layer makes, not the read. **No write is reachable from this action**: save/overwrite/create/delete/rename rules, setAsDefault, start/stopRealTimeDrc and the whole net-class / pad-pair / equal-length / differential-pair family are off the list. Focus discipline is `pcb.drc_check`'s: a non-PCB focus is refused with PAGE_MISMATCH and the focused document named (no auto doc.open — opening a board is the caller's job), and an absent member is reported as absent rather than as a value, so a board whose rule set could not be read never reads as a board with no rules.
sys.connector_status   connector  read    -                            The About box's own read-out, for a caller outside the editor: the connection state plus the lifecycle counters that tell an inert extension from a missing one — moduleBootstrapObserved (was the bundle evaluated at all?), activateObserved (was activate() dispatched?), evaluations (how many times), and the background watchdog's state (running | unavailable(reason) | not started), which is the difference between a window that recovers by itself in the background and one that waits for the user to bring it to the front. Read-only: it never starts, stops or reconnects anything. If no evaluation has published its runtime record, present=false says so rather than guessing.
sys.log_read           connector  read    types,since,pattern,limit,maxChars READ-ONLY: the host's own log panel, as text, via `sys_Log.sort(types?)`. It exists because the **V3** `sch_Drc.check` verbose answer held **aggregate counts only** (025 §0, measured: no detail), while 岳's log panel showed 22 warn lines of full text on 2026-10-04. (V4 enumerates its findings in the array itself — see `sch.drc_check`'s `items` — so the panel is no longer the only per-item source there.) **Measured live 2026-10-04 (111b, test/P1, 22 warns): an API-driven `sch.drc_check` writes NOTHING to sys_Log — neither with userInterface:false nor :true — so this action does NOT recover the per-item ERC text of a harness-run check; that wording still comes only from a human running DRC from the editor menu (which is what fills the panel; inferred from the panel format, not yet re-confirmed by a manual run). What the action verifiably does: read the panel back — extension diagnostics, openProject events, and any menu-run ERC text that is there. `sort` only: `export` is never called (it opens the editor's save dialog) and `clear` is never called (it destroys the evidence); `find` is unused because sort plus a client-side substring filter covers it. Lines cross the wire verbatim — no re-casing, trimming or wrapping.
sch.readback           connector  read    includePrimitives            Schematic components and a primitive subset, for a netlist view. Refused with PAGE_MISMATCH when the focused document is a PCB (527B): the read answers in whatever namespace it is named after, not in the focused page's, so a wrong-page call used to return a phantom row or die on `null`.
pcb.readback           connector  read    includePrimitives            PCB components and a primitive subset (pads / tracks / vias). Same PAGE_MISMATCH refusal as sch.readback, mirrored for a schematic page in front (527B).
export.screenshot      connector  read    fit                          Native editor image export of the current canvas, as base64 PNG.
export.render          connector  read    format,scope,ids,fileName    Render the *document* to an image file (base64) via sch_ManufactureData.getExportDocumentFile — the acceptance image. A viewport capture (export.screenshot) can return cached frames on this host, so it is never evidence. Scope can be the current page, a selection of primitives, or the whole project; a multi-page project may come back as a zip and the `format` field says which.
canvas.highlight       connector  read    uuids,color,clear,zoom       Mark primitives on the live canvas by uuid (review annotations).
sch.component_pins     connector  read    primitiveId                  Recon (read-only): the placed pins of one component, with geometry. The seventh path to a pin the six-path table had missed — sch_PrimitiveComponent.getAllPinsByPrimitiveId returns 器件引脚图元 (x/y/pinNumber/pinName/rotation/pinLength) for a PLACED component, @beta with no ADD-since-v4 marker. Decides whether F3 (drifted-part endpoint snapping) is implementable.
lib.device.get         connector  read    uuid,libraryUuid             Recon (read-only): one library device, dumped whole. Its association.symbol is the *library* symbol uuid that lib.symbol.get needs — the netlist's Symbol property is project-local and answers found:false there.
lib.device.search      connector  read    keyword,limit                Read-only: library device keyword candidates, each dumped. A search item carries association.footprint.uuid, so pairing it with lib.footprint.get answers 'which hit is really 0402?' by measurement.
lib.footprint.get      connector  read    uuid,libraryUuid             Read-only: one library footprint, dumped whole. Turns the netlist's footprint uuid back into the package name both sides can compare, and verifies a replacement part really is the package it claims.
sch.set_component_attribute connector  write   primitiveId,attributes,key,value,pageUuid Write schematic attributes on a placed component in ONE call, then read them back. modify()'s otherProperty REPLACES the whole map (measured: writing Value then Supplier Footprint kept only the second), so callers send attributes{} and the action merges first. `applied` means the read-back equals the target, never 'modify returned an object'.
lib.symbol.get         connector  read    uuid,libraryUuid             Recon (read-only): one library symbol, dumped whole. Answers whether the *library* path exposes pin geometry — the canvas path is measured dead (sch_PrimitivePin.getAll() empty, Symbol state {}, netlist has no coordinates), but nobody had looked here.
sch.netlist            connector  read    type                         The editor's own netlist export (sch_ManufactureData.getNetlistFile) — the ground-truth connectivity for draw verification.
sch.geometry           connector  read    bboxIds                      Full geometry of the open schematic page (wires with polylines, pins, net labels, components) — the readback fallback when the netlist export is unusable.
pcb.geometry           connector  read    bboxIds                      Read-only: the **measured** rendered bounding box of PCB primitives (`eda.pcb_Primitive.getPrimitivesBBox`, one call per id — the host answers a union box for a list). The PCB twin of `sch.geometry`'s `bboxIds` half: a board primitive's real extent is not in the file, so this is the only way to answer 「这块丝印压上焊盘了吗」 by measurement rather than by a font-width model.
sch.doc.new            connector  create  name,confirm                 Create a blank schematic page in the current project.
sch.doc.save           connector  write   -                            Save the project — required before the netlist export, which returns nothing for a never-saved project (measured).
sch.place_component    connector  write   lcsc,deviceUuid,libraryUuid,keyword,x,y,rotation,mirror,designator,pageUuid,timeoutMs Place a library device (resolved by LCSC part number, library uuid pair, or keyword search) on the current schematic page. Timeout-bounded and self-reporting: the first placement of a session can outrun its deadline and land anyway, so a miss reads the page back and says whether a part appeared.
sch.place_wire         connector  write   points,net,pageUuid          Place a wire polyline, optionally naming its net.
sch.place_netlabel     connector  write   x,y,net,pageUuid,timeoutMs   Place a net label. Timeout-bounded and self-reporting: the call races an 8 s deadline and, when the host hangs (measured on 3.2.186, reference issue #191), reads back whether the label landed anyway before failing — never retry blind.
sch.place_text         connector  write   x,y,content,rotation,color,fontSize,pageUuid Place a free text primitive next to a wire — the *decorative* signal-name fallback. `createNetLabel` (the only real net-label API) is documented 'ADD since EDA v4' and can never settle on the v3.2 host, so a signal name is drawn as text: visible to a reader, but NOT an electrical object. The response says `decorative: true`.
sch.place_power        connector  write   kind,net,x,y,rotation,mirror,pageUuid Place a power / ground net flag (a real library component placed by the editor, named with the given net).
sch.place_netport      connector  write   direction,net,x,y,rotation,mirror,pageUuid Place a net port (IN / OUT / BI) carrying a net name. The solver's LAST resort only: xianyuyijinban's rule bans I/O ports for signal naming — the draw flow names signals with label actions and never emits one.
sch.delete_primitives  connector  write   pageUuid,primitiveIds        Delete schematic primitives by id. The page's id index is built first (component / wire / text / pin — the classes the type package lets address by id; attribute primitives cannot be), so an id the page never held is reported, not guessed at. Honest partial result: deleted / notFound / failed.
pcb.delete_primitives  connector  write   pageUuid,primitiveIds        Delete PCB primitives by id — component / line / via / pad / pour, guarded against the focused PCB. Honest partial result, same shape as sch.delete_primitives.
sch.modify_primitive   connector  write   pageUuid,primitiveId,x,y,rotation,mirror Move / rotate / mirror one schematic primitive by id — pose only. The class comes from the page's id index; the pose keys are filtered through what that class's modify actually accepts (a wire has no pose in the type package and is refused). Returns the before/after pose for verification.
pcb.modify_primitive   connector  write   pageUuid,primitiveId,x,y,rotation,mirror Move / rotate one PCB primitive by id — pose only, same contract as sch.modify_primitive against the focused PCB.

usage: boardwise bridge [-h] [--port PORT]
                        {start,status,revoke,screenshot,export-fab,call,highlight,update-connector} ...

Live channel to a running EasyEDA Pro: a loopback daemon plus an editor
extension. Actions owned by 'daemon' are answered locally; 'connector' actions
are forwarded into the editor.

positional arguments:
  {start,status,revoke,screenshot,export-fab,call,highlight,update-connector}
    start               Run the daemon in the foreground.
    status              Report whether the daemon and connector are up.
    revoke              Forget the paired connector; the next one to connect is
                        trusted instead.
    screenshot          Export the current canvas as PNG.
    export-fab          Export the fab bundle (Gerber + pick-and-place + BOM +
                        manifest.json) into a directory. 012v2 §六.
    call                Call one connector action directly (probes and
                        diagnosis); --action NAME [--params JSON].
    highlight           Mark primitives on the live canvas.
    update-connector    Hot-update the running connector to a freshly built
                        bundle (sys.self_update): no uninstall, no re-import, no
                        editor restart — the editor page reloads itself after
                        the write.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --port PORT           Daemon port (default 61190).

DANGEROUS**: rewrite the **active** document's source text. The write half of

required and must be the active document (179's DOC_NOT_ACTIVE shape): the host
call takes the text and nothing else (declared arity 1), so it rewrites whatever
is in front. `risk=dangerous` puts it behind the create gate's choke point — the

connector read strict,userInterface,includeVerboseError READ-ONLY: the schematic
DRC, via sch_Drc.check(strict, userInterface, includeVerboseError). The answer's
shape changed between editor generations, and both are read (038 O3a/O3b): the
025 §0 measurement (V3) found **aggregate counts only** — `[{type:
'fatalError'|'error'|'warn', count}]`, the per-item detail going to the bottom
panel, which has no read interface; the V4.1.93 measurement (2026-10-31, two

primitives}` with no `count`, 519 of them. The connector normalises both:

still returned **verbatim** under `counts`; an entry with a numeric `count`

contributes 1, and anything else is counted in `unparsed` instead of folding in

focused document named. pcb.drc_check connector read

can read the shape the editor really produces; `counts` only describes what came
back, and whole groups are dropped (never cut in half) to stay inside

promises `undefined`, the host actually **throws** (a message-bus error — the
check publishes to the PCB canvas topic and nothing subscribes on a schematic
page), and both are reported as `checked: false` with the focused document named
— never as an empty result. Note that an *empty* PCB is not a clean board with
zero findings either: the test project's empty PCB answered one 'Netlist Error /
Import Changes'. pcb.drc_ruleset connector read maxChars,all READ-ONLY: the DRC
rule set in force on the focused PCB, via the read-side members of pcb_Drc —
getCurrentRuleConfigurationName(), getCurrentRuleConfiguration(),
getDefaultRuleConfigurationName(), getRealTimeDrcStatus() (`all: true` adds
getAllRuleConfigurations()). A PCB DRC result is a statement about a rule set,
so 025's leaves without these are half an answer. The values come back
**verbatim**, sanitised conservatively: functions dropped (they are the back-
references that make an editor object graph cyclic), `toJSON`-bearing objects
rendered through the host's own serialiser (a Date stays the instant it is),
cycles cut as '(cycle)' at the re-entry point; every cut is counted and named in
`notes`. **Nothing is compared** — whether a rule set matches the board's
process is a judgement the review layer makes, not the read. **No write is
reachable from this action**: save/overwrite/create/delete/rename rules,
setAsDefault, start/stopRealTimeDrc and the whole net-class / pad-pair / equal-
length / differential-pair family are off the list. Focus discipline is
`pcb.drc_check`'s: a non-PCB focus is refused with PAGE_MISMATCH and the focused
document named (no auto doc.open — opening a board is the caller's job), and an
absent member is reported as absent rather than as a value, so a board whose
rule set could not be read never reads as a board with no rules.

an inert extension from a missing one — moduleBootstrapObserved (was the bundle
evaluated at all?), activateObserved (was activate() dispatched?), evaluations

                        still answering).

                        back announcing the stored version.

edit.description: The M3 loop's middle: `edit plan` turns one finding into a ChangePlan (data, inspectable), `edit preview` re-checks it offline against the snapshot, `edit apply` executes it on the live canvas — one write, then a read-back, a save and a re-review. `--file` repairs one component's value (`param-value-mpn-match`, whose finding records a contradiction rather than a repair, so the direction is stated with it); the other kinds are reached by `--report` / `--insert` / `--move`, and a rule outside that table is refused by name. Exit 0 applied (or already applied) / 2 the promised effect is not on the board (a refused write, a read-back that disagrees, a save the editor refused, a re-review that still reports the finding) / 3 the page's state cannot be stated (a timeout or a dropped connection; nothing is retried) / 4 a precondition of the plan no longer holds, or the snapshot is stale / 5 the plan or the input is unusable.

  --file FILE           The .epro2 / .enet snapshot the plan is built against.
                        Required by the `--file` and `--report` ways in (it is
                        the snapshot's sha256 the plan carries); `--insert`
                        builds from the live page and records the live export's
                        own sha256 instead, so it refuses this flag rather than
                        quietly ignoring it.
  --rule RULE           Rule id whose finding the plan repairs (e.g. param-
                        value-mpn-match). Required except with `--insert`, which
                        has no rule to name (036).
  --designator DESIGNATOR

                        `--insert divider`, which anchors on a net (036).
  --after AFTER         The value to write. Required for `param-value-mpn-match`
                        unless the finding carries a suggestion of its own,
                        which since 052 §2.1 it does not: that finding records a
                        contradiction whose two repairs are fixing Value to the
                        MPN's decoded value or swapping in a part that matches
                        the design value, and the direction is the operator's to
                        state (--after names the value of the first).
  --direction {value,mpn}
                        Which field the repair writes (052 §2.1), for the --file
                        path only: `value` repairs the board's Value field and
                        still needs --after <value>; `mpn` would repair the
                        MPN/LCSC field, whose change kind this build does not
                        have, so it is refused and says so. Neither flag leaves
                        the direction unstated, and a plan is not built then —
                        the MPN-decoded value is a candidate, not the answer
                        (048).

                        stdout).
  --json PATH           Write the machine-readable result.
  --view {schematic,pcb}

                        the view the 011-family rules are written against; a
                        schematic-only export's pcb view is empty).

                        running the rule: the finding there carries the anchor,
                        the supply pin, the net and the recipe (`decap-required-
                        caps` findings only). Needs --lcsc and a live editor

                        `sch.geometry`) — `edit plan --help`, §029-a.

                        carry several findings for one designator under one rule

                        one decap row per supply pin — and the selector will not
                        pick one for you: with more than one match it refuses
                        and names the pins. Required then, optional otherwise;
                        when given it must match exactly one finding.

                        the plan is refused: an unverified recipe is not
                        something to place silently.

                        geometry on the page — a divider hanging off nothing is

                        of 5-unit grid steps, the group must be parts (not a
                        sheet frame), and every wire attached to the group is

                              [--view {schematic,pcb}] [--project NAME_OR_UUID]

target is still there with the value the plan expects. Exit 4 for a stale
snapshot or a target that moved; nothing is written, ever. --file is required:
the plan carries the input's hash, not its path, so without the file there is
nothing to check.

apply.description: The four protections, in order: re-read the page and refuse a stale snapshot; write exactly one key on exactly one primitive; verify with the action's own read-back **and** an independent geometry read; and treat a timeout or a dropped connection as unknown — read the page back and never retry. Then `sch.doc.save` and a re-review: for `add-component` the live project is re-exported and the rule re-run (029-d §②), for `component-value` the snapshot `--file` is re-read. A repeated run recognises the work is already done and writes nothing (exit 0, already_applied).

install-skill.description: Writes the SKILL.md this build carries where the agent reads it: ~/.kimi-code/skills/boardwise/SKILL.md for Kimi Code (override the directory with BOARDWISE_SKILL_HOME) and ~/.claude/skills/boardwise/SKILL.md for Claude Code (override with BOARDWISE_SKILL_HOME_CLAUDE). --harness picks one side; the default is all of them, because this toolchain is meant to work under either agent and one of them having no SOP is exactly the state that is impossible to notice from the outside. Idempotent: an identical file says 'already current' and is left alone. A *different* file is backed up to SKILL.md.bak-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS> first — never silently overwritten, and never overwritten by a second install on the same day either. --uninstall removes the installed copy from the selected harnesses, and each directory when it empties. --agent writes nothing: it prints the absolute path of the bundled SKILL.md and a paragraph to hand to an agent this build knows nothing about (Codex, Hermes, ...), whose skill directory *it* knows and we would only be guessing at (062).

draw.help:
usage: boardwise draw [-h] [--from FROM_FILE] [--spec SPEC] [--golden GOLDEN]
                      [--yes] [--screenshot SCREENSHOT] [--overrides OVERRIDES]
                      [--render RENDER] [--solver]
                      [--naming {auto,wire,text,label,none}]
                      [--port-meta PORT_META] [--library LIBRARY]
                      {compile,plan,apply,discard,lint,propose,islands} ...

positional arguments:
  {compile,plan,apply,discard,lint,propose,islands}
    compile             Offline: compile two specs into legal drawings, rank
                        them, and write the previews (053 stage B, task 054).
    plan                Offline (or page-bound): one candidate -> the ChangePlan
                        a human authorises.
    apply               On the live page: guard, land the drawing, read it back,
                        save, render.
    discard             On the live page: delete exactly one plan's drawing,
                        identity-checked.
    lint                Read-only readability lint of one page: nine geometric
                        predicates (text-on-wire, text-on-text, text-on-part,
                        wire-through-part, duplicate-annotation, crossings,
                        label-wire-clearance, flag orientation, board fill),
                        findings by severity (task 111).
    propose             Offline: one DesignIntent contract -> one
                        PresentationSpec draft (module list + flow + roles,
                        109).
    islands             Offline: propose the islands a spec has not declared,
                        and write a judged proposal into it (530E).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --from FROM_FILE      Path to the golden .epro2 whose connectivity is the
                        design input.
  --spec SPEC           Path to a board spec. The design is assembled from its
                        block templates; --from is then only used for the
                        double-check.
  --golden GOLDEN       With --spec: the .epro2 to double-check the spec netlist
                        against **before** anything is created. A mismatch
                        aborts the run.
  --yes                 Skip the execution gate (print the plan and go).
  --screenshot SCREENSHOT
                        Where to write the post-draw canvas screenshot (PNG
                        path).
  --overrides OVERRIDES
                        Golden-corrections sidecar (JSON). Default: the file
                        next to the golden fixture, `<stem>.overrides.json`. The
                        fixture itself is evidence and is never edited; the
                        sidecar carries the corrections and every hit is
                        reported with its provenance.
  --render RENDER       Where to write the acceptance image — an `export.render`
                        document render (PNG). A viewport screenshot is NOT
                        evidence (cached frames).
  --solver              Use the generic layout solver instead of replaying the
                        golden page's own geometry (the default).
  --naming {auto,wire,text,label,none}
                        How signal nets are named (default: auto). auto: name a
                        signal net only when it is long or cross-page —
                        everything else is read off its wires (a net label is an
                        electrical net port in EasyEDA, so naming everything
                        buries connections); wire: the wire carries the net name
                        only; text: wire plus a decorative text label beside
                        every signal net (visible, not an electrical object —
                        the report says so); label: the native net-label API
                        (needs an EDA v4 host; dormant); none: no signal names
                        at all. Rails always keep their flags.
  --port-meta PORT_META
                        Spec mode only: the port-metadata sidecar the pre-draw
                        validation reads (default:
                        blocklib/blocks.portmeta.json, same convention as
                        `validate`). Without it the levels and power-tree gates
                        answer "cannot tell", which refuses the draw.
  --library LIBRARY     Spec mode only: curated part library a `part` reference
                        in the spec can cite (default: none; a part citation
                        without a library is undecidable, which refuses the
                        draw).

compile.description: The compiler that turns a CircuitSpec + PresentationSpec + a symbol library into the legal drawings that survived its hard gate, best first — at most eight, and one or two is a normal success. It prints the ranking (the layers are compared, never summed), the four refusal categories with the action that would fix each one, and writes one SVG preview and one LayoutPlan JSON per candidate. Nothing here touches the editor. Exit 0 at least one candidate / 5 the compiler refused or an input could not be read.

usage: boardwise draw compile [-h] --circuit PATH --presentation PATH
                              --profiles PATH [--page-box X0,Y0,X1,Y1]
                              [--out DIR] [--json PATH] [--intent PATH]

The compiler that turns a CircuitSpec + PresentationSpec + a symbol library into
the legal drawings that survived its hard gate, best first — at most eight, and
one or two is a normal success. It prints the ranking (the layers are compared,
never summed), the four refusal categories with the action that would fix each
one, and writes one SVG preview and one LayoutPlan JSON per candidate. Nothing
here touches the editor. Exit 0 at least one candidate / 5 the compiler refused
or an input could not be read.

options:

  --circuit PATH        The CircuitSpec JSON.
  --presentation PATH   The PresentationSpec JSON (the grammar to draw the
                        circuit in).
  --profiles PATH       The symbol library: `{"profiles": [SymbolProfile, …]}`,
                        a bare list, or a symbolRef -> SymbolProfile mapping.

                        geometry the layout is drawn against.
  --page-box X0,Y0,X1,Y1
                        The sheet the drawing must fit in, in canvas units.
                        Given, the drawing is anchored at that page's own top-
                        left corner, so the plan's coordinates are canvas
                        coordinates a landing can use.

                        outputs/054_drawcompile).
  --json PATH           Write the machine-readable result.

                        090 A1) — today the branch order of a `power-entry`
                        drawing and the core of an `ic-periphery` one: a

                        rail places it nearest the inlet, and a `blocks[]` entry
                        whose parts name exactly one multi-pin part of the
                        drawing says which part it is arranged around, so the

                        alike. Explicit path only: this command compiles before
                        anything names a project, so the user-level default
                        (`~/.boardwise/design-intent/<uuid>.json`) has no uuid
                        to be found from.
                        `PresentationSpec.modules[].branchOrder` still outranks

apply.description: Land one `draw-module` plan: the guards first (both spec digests, the layout digest, the library geometry table, the page's identity and its primitive census) with nothing written if any of them fails; then the plan's own postconditions read on the page (satisfied = already_applied, zero writes); then the parts, a pin read-back against the plan's expected offsets *before* any wire, the wires and the rail flags; then both verification legs (the editor's own netlist and the canvas), the range on a fresh export and the findings' one-way rule graded by severity (an ERROR always stops the save, a WARN unless --force, an INFO never); then the save and the render. Exit 0 applied (or already applied) / 2 the promised effect is not there / 3 the state cannot be stated or the read-back disagrees / 4 a guard refused / 5 the plan is unusable.

usage: boardwise draw apply [-h] [--page UUID] [--new-page] [--page-name NAME]
                            [--expect-census SHA256] [--circuit PATH]
                            [--presentation PATH] [--profiles PATH]
                            [--layout PATH] [--keep-names] [--render PATH]
                            [--out DIR] [--json PATH] [--force]
                            [--page-box X0,Y0,X1,Y1] [--project NAME_OR_UUID]
                            [--instance INSTANCE_ID] [--port PORT]
                            plan

Land one `draw-module` plan: the guards first (both spec digests, the layout
digest, the library geometry table, the page's identity and its primitive
census) with nothing written if any of them fails; then the plan's own
postconditions read on the page (satisfied = already_applied, zero writes); then
the parts, a pin read-back against the plan's expected offsets *before* any
wire, the wires and the rail flags; then both verification legs (the editor's
own netlist and the canvas), the range on a fresh export and the findings' one-
way rule graded by severity (an ERROR always stops the save, a WARN unless
--force, an INFO never); then the save and the render. Exit 0 applied (or
already applied) / 2 the promised effect is not there / 3 the state cannot be
stated or the read-back disagrees / 4 a guard refused / 5 the plan is unusable.

positional arguments:
  plan                  The ChangePlan JSON `draw plan` wrote.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --page UUID           The page to land on, when the plan is not bound to one.
                        Required for a repeat run (`already_applied`) unless the
                        plan carries its page.
  --new-page            Create a page for this drawing (`sch.doc.new`, a
                        `create` action), when the plan is not bound to one and
                        `--page` is not given. Refused (exit 5) when either is —
                        a run cannot both land on a settled page and create one,
                        and the flag is never ignored. The host ignores the name
                        (pit 24), so the page's uuid is the identity and it is
                        confirmed against the listing afterwards.
  --page-name NAME      The name handed to `sch.doc.new` (cosmetic: the host
                        ignores it). Read only where a page is created; a run
                        that creates none says so.
  --expect-census SHA256
                        The page census this run must find before it writes —
                        the digest a previous run's report quoted. This is 054's
                        C5 guard for a plan built offline: a page somebody
                        changed by hand then refuses (exit 4, zero writes)
                        instead of being drawn over.
  --circuit PATH        The CircuitSpec JSON to re-digest for the stale guard.
  --presentation PATH   The PresentationSpec JSON to re-digest for the stale
                        guard.
  --profiles PATH       The symbol library, for the library-geometry guard (C6).
  --layout PATH         The LayoutPlan JSON to re-digest for the layout guard.

add.description: Two jobs in one flow. Identity only (`boardwise parts add <MPN> --lcsc C1234`): append a candidate entry — no category, no facts, facts_trust candidate, provenance.kind manual-curation. With facts (`--facts <file.json>` / repeated `--fact KEY=JSON`): write those facts onto the entry — the one already on the shelf when the identity exists (that is the candidate `parts fetch` left behind), otherwise a new one — and `--verified` is the engineer's explicit declaration that they were checked, which is what makes them drive rules. Without `--verified` the facts are a candidate's claim and drive nothing. `--verified` is never implied. A duplicate insisted on without facts is refused (exit 2) and points at `parts show`. The file is edited at the JSON-document level so existing entries keep their exact bytes, backed up to a .tmp sibling first, and re-parsed with the real validator before the write is called done. `--resolve` (187c) fills the two uuids the verified gate demands from the online bridge — one command from a datasheet to a landed entry.

usage: boardwise parts add [-h] --lcsc LCSC [--key KEY] [--facts FILE]
                           [--fact KEY=JSON] [--verified] [--force]
                           [--category CATEGORY] [--device-uuid DEVICE_UUID]
                           [--library-uuid LIBRARY_UUID] [--resolve]
                           [--library LIBRARY] [--json PATH]
                           mpn

append a candidate entry — no category, no facts, facts_trust candidate,
provenance.kind manual-curation. With facts (`--facts <file.json>` / repeated
`--fact KEY=JSON`): write those facts onto the entry — the one already on the
shelf when the identity exists (that is the candidate `parts fetch` left
behind), otherwise a new one — and `--verified` is the engineer's explicit
declaration that they were checked, which is what makes them drive rules.

(exit 2) and points at `parts show`. The file is edited at the JSON-document
level so existing entries keep their exact bytes, backed up to a .tmp sibling

`--resolve` (187c) fills the two uuids the verified gate demands from the online

options:

  --lcsc LCSC           Its LCSC C-code (e.g. C2977777).

                        accepted as it stands. Every fact is validated by the

accept-unknown.description: 191A: the datasheet gate's second exit. A part the shelf cannot judge stops the review (`unreviewed_parts` → `verdict: incomplete`); the other way out is to **state that it need not be judged**. The acceptance is written into the DesignIntent contract (`acceptedUnknown[]`: part / reason / who / when / board), which is the file `checkup` already reads — so the next run moves that part out of `unreviewed_parts` into the report's `accepted_unknown[]`, stops being `incomplete` because of it, and still says 「另有 N 颗工程师接受未审」 in the quotable conclusion. `--reason` is mandatory (an acceptance with no reason would be a silent pass); `--revoke` takes one back. A contract entry whose part the drawing no longer has is kept and marked `stale` rather than deleted. Exit 0 written / 2 unusable input, a missing `--reason`, or a `--revoke` with nothing to revoke.

hunt.description: The batch half of `parts fetch` (520). Every component of a board is classified into one of three channels — a valid 立创 C-number (asked about via the product detail API, which sends the C-number and nothing else), an MPN only (needs a search engine), or no identity at all (the engineer's own job). Whatever comes back as a PDF is checked for the PDF magic before the extractor sees it: a landing page or a 404 is `download-failed`, never a text dump that reads as 'the datasheet says nothing'. Four artefacts land in --out: hunt-report.json (every part and its outcome), hunt-plan.json (the parts that need a search, as {designator, mpn, query} only), hunt-report.md (the one-page read) and hunt-audit.jsonl (one line per outbound call — the evidence that only a C-number or an MPN left the machine). `--apply answers.json` is the second stage: hand-found URLs come back in and go through the same download / extract / land path. Nothing here verifies anything: entries land with facts_verified: false, so 喂 PDF ≠ 清闸 still holds. Exit 0 report written / 2 the input or an answers file cannot be read.

classify.description: 523/527D: the first-class route to a shelf entry's `category`. `parts hunt --apply-facts` can write facts that drive calculations, but until this command existed nothing could set the class those facts are judged against — `rules.facts._category_state` answers UNKNOWN for an entry with no category whatever else is on it — so the only way was editing blocklib/parts.json by hand. The word must come from the shelf's own table (`core.parts.CATEGORY_VOCABULARY`); anything else is exit 2 with the legal families listed, because the table is extended by decision and never by typo. `--from` + `--page` + `--quote` **together** are the evidence: the quote goes through 521's gate (at least 10 characters / 3 words, whole-word, verbatim on the page it cites, checked against a document on disk — no network), and the entry is written `category_trust: machine_verified`. A category is a **conclusion**, so 522's dividing line applies: the machine tier unlocks the calculation rules and no connectivity / safety rule. With no evidence at all the class is written as the **human** tier (`verified`, the default — no key in the file) and the output says so. Only the entry's class keys move: `category`, `category_trust`, and — with evidence — `category_provenance` (527D2), which keeps the three flags on the shelf so the citation survives the terminal (a re-sign without evidence takes it back off): every other byte of the shelf is preserved, the file is backed up to a .tmp sibling and re-parsed with the real validator. Exit 0 written / 2 a word outside the table, an entry the shelf does not have (this command never creates one), or evidence that does not hold.
